fields.description:
Add an `mcp` autodeploy target to `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` implementing the ADR 0079
amendment's blue-green pointer-swap, so on-box `rebar-mcp` tracks `origin/main` without killing
an in-flight certified op (eliminates bug 7b4a). Scope: MCP deploy path only (edge = esok,
secrets = avians); no new timer (existing `rebar-autodeploy.timer`→`.service`).

## Approach (blue-green, ADR deft-evolutive-mosasaur / 0079)
Model on the LOCAL `origin/main` updater (`sticky-genetic-narwhal`): immutable release + atomic
pointer swap + graceful retire, NOT stop-and-drain. On MCP source change:
1. Build + tag immutable `compose-mcp:<target-sha>` (`docker compose build mcp`).
2. **Memory pre-check BEFORE the 2x overlap** (t4g.large 8 GiB): `MemAvailable` (`/proc/meminfo`,
   MB) `< MCP_MEM_MIN_MB` (default 1024) ABORTS — `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT`, backoff, no second
   container. Unreadable fails OPEN; `MCP_MEM_AVAILABLE_MB` overrides for tests.
3. Start a NEW container alongside old via **`docker run -d`** on a FREE A/B host port (see Run
   mechanism).
4. Health-check the NEW `/health` 200 within `MCP_HEALTH_TIMEOUT` (default 120). On failure:
   `docker rm -f` new, leave OLD include UNCHANGED, `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` `mcp-unhealthy`, backoff,
   exit 1.
5. **Atomically flip the nginx `/mcp/` upstream**: back up the include, write
   `server 127.0.0.1:<newport>;` to a dotfile temp NOT matching the `mcp-upstream*.conf` glob,
   `mv` (atomic rename) over `/etc/nginx/mcp-upstream.conf`, `nginx -t`, `nginx -s reload`. On
   failure: RESTORE backup, `docker rm -f` new, backoff, exit 1. DONE at the reload.
6. **Retire the OLD container**, retaining newest `MCP_RELEASES_KEEP` (default 1). Teardown is a
   GRACEFUL `docker stop --time 1260` (SIGTERM), which triggers the container's OWN bounded
   self-drain (`_mcp_health.run_http_with_grace`: stop intake, wait `in_flight`→0 up to
   `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS`=1200s, exit; compose `stop_grace_period`=1260s) — NEVER
   `docker rm -f`/SIGKILL a serving container, so no in-flight certified op is killed. The stop is issued
   in the BACKGROUND so the tick never waits on drain; exited containers are then `docker rm`'d
   and their A/B ports freed. If the managed count exceeds `MCP_RELEASES_CAP`
   (default 3) — too many still draining/holding ports — emit `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` instead
   of forcing (also the port-exhaustion guard). Since `autodeploy.sh` exits
   early when up-to-date, also run `mcp_retire_sweep` on the no-op tick so exited containers are
   reaped as they drain.

## Run mechanism + managed set
`docker compose up mcp` pins `8091` and would collide, so the NEW container starts via **`docker
run -d`** from `compose-mcp:<sha>` (helper `mcp_run_new`) on a FREE blue-green HOST
port `-p 127.0.0.1:<newport>:8091` (container port stays 8091): `newport` = whichever of
`MCP_PORT_A=8092`/`MCP_PORT_B=8093` is NOT currently bound by a managed container (8091 is
RESERVED for the compose-original). If BOTH A and B are bound by un-reclaimable containers, the
deploy does NOT start a colliding 3rd — it emits `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` + backoff and starts
nothing. So managed ports = EXACTLY {8091,8092,8093} = `MCP_RELEASES_CAP=3` (cap = port pool). `mcp_run_new` reproduces the compose `mcp:` service EXACTLY —
`--env-file .env`, every `REBAR_MCP_*`/`REBAR_OPCERT_*` var with compose's literal
`${VAR:-default}` values (`docker run` does NOT interpolate), the two `:ro` secret mounts,
`--restart always`, `--stop-timeout 1260`; the compose-parity oracle pins this set. The managed
MCP set (sweep/cap counts it) = names matching `MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX` (`rebar-mcp`) OR
`MCP_COMPOSE_CONTAINER` (`compose-mcp-1`); at boot `compose-up.sh` brings up `compose-mcp-1` on
8091 (seed include→8091), retired gracefully like any other (autodeploy never `docker compose up
mcp`).

## Change detection + blast radius
`MCP_PATHS='src/rebar infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp infra/compose/docker-compose.yml uv.lock pyproject.toml'`
— esok's canonical `mcp:` compose-comment set. Diffed `deployed..target` it triggers ONLY `mcp`;
`src/rebar`+`docker-compose.yml` are shared with `BOT_PATHS`, so a shared change triggers BOTH
targets in independent `if changed` blocks. `gerrit` untouched (gerrit-id assert).
`flock` still serializes.

## Failure + backoff
The `mcp` branch failure is FATAL like `review-bot` (`record_backoff_failure` + `exit 1`), so
`deployed-sha` is not advanced and the deploy retries next tick. For a shared change review-bot
runs first; its idempotent rebuild just repeats until mcp also succeeds.

## Alerting (marker → observability → CloudWatch → SNS; NO direct SNS publish)
autodeploy.sh has no `sns:Publish` path and must not gain one. Like every existing autodeploy
alert: a countable `marker AUTODEPLOY_MCP_* {json}` → `observability.sh`
`publish_autodeploy_marker_delta` → a dimensionless `rebar/host` metric → a terraform
`aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` → `aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn`. Adds tokens `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP`
+ `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT` (distinct from `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`); two marker-delta calls (+ offset
files) → `rebar/host:mcp_retire_cap` + `rebar/host:mcp_mem_abort`; two alarms mirroring
`monitoring_autodeploy.tf`'s 900s/2-of-4/Sum>0/notBreaching shape.

## Portability (`project.portability`)
Trigger is the on-box systemd/launchd timer polling the git mirror — operation-linked, not CI;
flip/retire run in-process. Works with any/no CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Tier: **real subprocess/bash integration, temp git repos + fake docker/nginx**. Tests stub
  the box binaries onto PATH and run the REAL `autodeploy.sh` in `tests/scripts/`. Oracles:
  - Change detection (REAL temp git repo, two commits, asserted via the docker call log): an
    MCP-only change (touch `Dockerfile.mcp`) triggers `mcp` and NO review-bot/gerrit rebuild; a
    review-bot-only change (`Dockerfile.reviewbot`) does the inverse; a shared `src/rebar` change
    triggers BOTH independently.
  - Cutover order start-new → health → flip → retire (via the call log); returns success
    WITHOUT waiting on `in_flight` (with `in_flight>0` on OLD it still flips and exits 0).
  - Retire is GRACEFUL: the OLD container is torn down with `docker stop` (SIGTERM self-drain),
    NEVER `docker rm -f`; an `in_flight>0` OLD container is `docker stop`'d (drains, not
    SIGKILLed) and the deploy returns before its drain finishes; over `MCP_RELEASES_CAP`
    `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP` is emitted with no forced kill.
  - Port exhaustion: with BOTH A and B bound by `in_flight>0` containers, a new MCP change does
    NOT `docker run -p` on an occupied port (no 3rd container); `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP`
    emitted, backoff recorded.
  - Memory pre-check: `MCP_MEM_AVAILABLE_MB < MCP_MEM_MIN_MB` ABORTS — no second container started,
    `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_MEM_ABORT` emitted, backoff recorded, include unchanged.
  - Health-check OR nginx reload failure leaves the OLD include byte-identical
    (`AUTODEPLOY_ERROR`, backoff, `deployed-sha` not advanced); a retry next healthy tick flips it.
  - `gerrit` container id UNCHANGED across an mcp deploy (blast radius).
  - Compose parity: a test parses the `mcp:` service in `docker-compose.yml` and asserts
    `mcp_run_new`'s `docker run` env keys+values and `:ro` mounts match it — drift guard, since
    `/health` is auth-independent and cannot catch a wrong `REBAR_MCP_AUTH_*`/`ALLOWED_HOSTS`.
- [x] observability.sh publishes `rebar/host:mcp_retire_cap` + `rebar/host:mcp_mem_abort`; two
  terraform CloudWatch alarms route them to `aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn` (mirror
  `monitoring_autodeploy.tf`).

## Compat / rollback
Additive (new `if changed "$MCP_PATHS"` block + no-op sweep); other targets unchanged (existing autodeploy
tests stay green); ADRs 0079/0104 document it. Rollback = revert the additions AND
reset the include to `server 127.0.0.1:8091;` (edge points back at compose-managed 8091).

Depends on: deft-evolutive-mosasaur, esok.
